description:
Digital to Wave 2 unified is a SYNTHETIC unified verdict, in Python (3.11–3.13), for the claims in Mun Seok Lee's preprint Digital to Wave: LGD In Situ Wave Memory-Human Wave Integrated Interface-Metaverse Hologram- Wave Affective AI (Part II, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21947108). The preprint supplies the numbers; the computation, pass/fail criterion and tests are this project's own. Its author has not reviewed or endorsed this software.

What is included

  • The Fourier-duality joint bound: the Abbe diffraction limit (position space) and the relativistic de Broglie wavelength (momentum space) recomputed from the paper's own numbers, then the count of lattice sites satisfying BOTH at once -- zero, for every macroscopic mass and THz frequency.
  • An aggregator with five pieces (diffraction, de Broglie, joint, analog calibration robustness, spooky stability), one unified verdict (FAIL), and a benefits manifest with a reusable template (claim, Abbe, de Broglie, joint, bounded calibration, noisy-copy spooky, verdict) for testing other wave-memory claims.
  • A pytest suite (5 tests) and a one-page report with the symmetry, the numbers, the verdict and the honest caveats.

Results (SYNTHETIC)

  • Unified verdict: FAIL. Diffraction best case 301 MB readable vs 79.6 ZB claimed (short by 2.65 × 1014); de Broglie most generous case short by 1.68 × 1019; joint count 0 sites; bounded calibration buys 0.0223 orders; spooky 0.99999995, verdict stable 5/5.

Limits

No physical, biological or safety claim is made. This is a classical-physics bound applied to the paper's own numbers, not an experiment. Fourier duality is the known wave principle, not a new physical law. The illustrative product of the two shortfalls (~4.45 × 1033) is shown only for scale; the rigorous statements are the joint count (0) and the logical AND.
title: Digital to Wave 2 unified: Fourier duality unifies the Abbe and de Broglie falsifications of Part II
